items.summary: Supreme Court Justice Sandeep Mehta has asked Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant to appoint a Chief Justice from another State to head the Rajasthan High Court "with immediate effect". In letters dated August 2, August 10 and August 17 accessed by Bar & Bench , Justice Mehta has accused acting Chief Justice Sanjeev Prakash Sharma of manipulating case listings in favour of rich litigants and misusing his administrative powers ahead of his retirement, due later next month. Justice Sharma was appointed as Rajasthan High Court judge in November 2016 and transferred to the Patna High Court in 2022. When he sought repatriation on health grounds, the Collegium headed by then Chief Justice of India DY Chandrachud declined the request in March 2023 and sent him instead to the Punjab and Haryana High Court. In May 2025, a fresh Collegium resolution recommended his return to Rajasthan. He went on to become the acting Chief Justice, a post Justice Mehta's letter says he has now held "for more than last 10 months." Justice Mehta's letters draw on a recent Supreme Court observation made by a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi in an unrelated case. They had flagged a growing trend of judges passing orders for extraneous considerations on the eve of retirement, and judges attempting to "hit sixes" before retiring. Justice Sharma seems to be possessed of a licence to hit sixes ever since the day on which he took over as the Acting Chief Justice, Justice Mehta has written. As evidence, the letters cite two division bench orders of the Rajasthan High Court. items.title: Patiala House court rejects Delhi Race Club's plea against order to vacate its Lutyens' Delhi premises
items.summary: A Delhi court on Tuesday refused to stay the government order of August 11 directing Delhi Race Club to vacate its Lutyens Delhi Premises in 15 days. Delhi Race Club is a century-old horse-racing institution located on Central Golf Link Road opposite the Prime Minister's official residence. Principal District & Sessions Judge (PDSJ) Pitamber Dutt of the Patiala House Courts dismissed the application filed by the Club seeking interim stay of the eviction order passed against it by the Estate Officer under the Public Premises (Eviction of Unauthorised Occupants) Act. “In view of the above facts and circumstances, I am of the considered view that appellant has failed to make a prima facie case for stay of the impugned order dated 11.08.2026 passed by the Ld. Estate Officer in case No.ESO/11/3(1)/2026 titled as Union of India Vs. Delhi Race Club. Accordingly, the application filed by the applicant/appellant for interim stay is dismissed,” the Court said. Appearing for the club, Senior Advocate Suhail Dutt had argued that the Estate Officer's order dated August 11 violated principles of natural justice, as the Club was not supplied a copy of the plaint despite repeated requests. He also contended that the proceedings were barred by res judicata - a legal principle that bars reopening of a case already decided - since an earlier show cause notice from 1999 had been quashed by the Delhi High Court. Dutt further said that continued payment of rent and a lease-extension deposit made in 2013 amounted to renewal of the lease. items.title: Transgender person moves Kerala High Court alleging denial of entry to Sabarimala
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Monday sought the State government's response to a plea filed by a transgender devotee alleging denial of permission to enter Sabarimala temple due to her gender [Sathyashri Sharmila Rehemathali v State of Kerala & ors]. A bench of Justice Gopinath P and Justice S Manu issued notice to the State and posted the matter for further consideration on September 3. Justice Gopinath P and Justice S Manu The petition was filed by Sathyashri Sharmila Rehemathali, who identifies as a transgender woman and claims that she is a devote and a regular pilgrim to Sabarimala. According to the petition, Sharmila reached Pamba on August 20 to get Lord Ayyappa's darshan, after observing the required Vratham and carrying her Irumudi (sacred rituals undertaken by devotees). However, around 3:30 PM, she was stopped during a police inspection near the Pamba Ganapathi Temple and informed that she would not be permitted to proceed uphill because she was a transgender person. As per the petition, officers at the Pamba Police Station told her that the Travancore Devaswom Board had instructed the police not to permit transgender persons to proceed to Sabarimala. Sharmila asked the authorities to show her the written order, circular or notification, imposing such a restriction, but was told that the document could not be shown to her. She further pointed out that she had previously visited the temple on January 3 and April 15 and had been permitted to enter the temple and complete her pilgrimage. The petitioner therefore approached the Court, challenging the sudden restriction on her entry to the temple solely on account of her transgender identity. As per the plea, Section 3(e) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 prohibits denial of or unfair treatment in access to public places and religious institution. The petitioner has sought, among other reliefs, permission to undertake the pilgrimage to Sabarimala and offer prayers, besides direction to the State government to disclose and publish any circular or notification that restricts the entry of transgender devotees. She also specifically sought permission to visit Sabarimala on August 26, for Thiruvonam, to fulfil an offering to the deity though no such order was passed by the Court. The petitioner was represented by advocates Padma Lakshmi and Aleena Dileepkumar. Standing counsel G Biju appeared for the Travancore Devaswom Board. items.title: CPI hits out at Pinarayi over Deputy Leader of Opposition row
items.summary: The CPI has stepped up its criticism of CPI(M) leader and Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan over his reported decision to nominate a CPI(M) leader as Deputy Leader of the Opposition in the Kerala Assembly. CPI said the move violates coalition norms and the principles of Left politics. In an article published in the CPI mouthpiece Janayugam , party assistant secretary Sathyan Mokeri said the decision cannot be taken unilaterally by the Leader of the Opposition as discussions between the CPI and CPI(M) were still underway. “The statement made by the Leader of the Opposition Pinarayi Vijayan on the issue of the Deputy Leader of the Opposition can only be viewed as a complete violation of coalition etiquette and as an absence of the political ethics that must be upheld in coalition politics,” Mokeri wrote. The CPI had proposed the creation of the Deputy Leader of the Opposition post following the LDF's defeat in the Assembly elections, with the aim of strengthening the coalition's collective functioning, he said. Mokeri questioned Pinarayi's reported statement that he would decide on the Deputy Leader and send the nomination to the Speaker. “The issue of the Deputy Leader of the Opposition is a political matter. The Leader of the Opposition cannot take a decision on it on his own,” he said. Mokeri also pointed to recent discussions between LDF convenor TP Ramakrishnan and CPI state secretary Binoy Viswam, following which it was agreed that the Deputy Leader issue should not obstruct the functioning of the front or the convening of an LDF meeting. The subsequent LDF meeting decided to focus on strengthening the front and work collectively for victory in the bye-elections to 38 local self-government seats across 12 districts, Mokeri said. Against this backdrop, he questioned the rationale behind Pinarayi making a public statement on the Deputy Leader issue. “What prompted the Leader of the Opposition to make a statement that could weaken the LDF?” Mokeri asked. items.title: Tamil Nadu govt to explore industrial projects on land acquired for Parandur airport
items.summary: Follow TNM’s WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. The Tamil Nadu government will explore using land acquired for the now-scrapped Parandur greenfield airport project for alternative industrial projects, Industries Minister S Keerthana told the Assembly on Tuesday, August 25. Speaking during the debate on the Industries, Investment Promotion and Commerce, Keerthana said the government would explore industrial projects that do not affect the environment or the livelihoods of people in the region. Such projects would help create employment opportunities and promote economic growth in Parandur, she said. Her statement came a day after Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay announced in the Assembly that the proposed Parandur airport project would be scrapped. Keerthana said the acquired land could be used for other public purposes under Clause 99 of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, which permits a change in land-use purpose in case of unforeseen circumstances. Energy Resources and Law Minister CTR Nirmal Kumar said the government had acquired 1,802 acres for the proposed airport, which was 48% of the total land required, and the land could be considered for other public purposes. The airport project required 5,846 acres, of which 3,274 acres was patta land and 1,972 acres was government land, Nirmal Kumar said. He rejected claims that 90% of the required land had already been acquired. Of the 1,972 acres classified as government land, 1,558 acres comprised waterbodies, he added. Nirmal Kumar said no land had been acquired in Ekanapuram, Karai, Thandalam and Siruvalur, where residents had opposed the project. The project had also not received environmental clearance, he added. ‘Chennai airport be expanded’ The government has said it will identify a new site for the second airport while expanding the existing Chennai airport at Meenambakkam. Nirmal Kumar said the existing airport can currently handle 30 million passengers annually. Its capacity will increase to 35 million after the ongoing construction of Terminal 3 is completed and to 55 million once the proposed Terminal 5 becomes operational. Her father, Ankathi Rajesham was also arrested. Ankathi Manasa’s body was discovered after locals noticed a foul smell coming from a car parked near the agricultural market checkpost on August 21. The police, who were alerted by the village secretary, found the body wrapped in a blanket inside the vehicle. An Aadhaar card recovered from the car helped establish the woman’s identity. Yadelli Vinod Kumar (34) was taken into custody on August 24 by a special police team from the outskirts of Elkathurthi. Rajesham was subsequently arrested on Monday night. According to police, Manasa and Vinod were childhood friends and were in a romantic relationship. Vinod also knew Manasa’s family well. Preliminary investigation suggests that the two had an argument at Vinod’s room in neighbouring Karimnagar district on August 18. Police said Manasa had reportedly been insisting that he marry her. During questioning, Vinod allegedly told police that he had informed Manasa’s father, Ankathi Rajesham, about the dispute. He further claimed that Rajesham told him that Manasa was also causing problems for the family and asked him to “do something” about the situation. Upon further investigation, police learnt that Rajesham had asked Vinod to kill Manasa for bringing ‘dishonour to the family'. Manasa had been divorced twice before and was living with her parents. Police also said she had epilepsy and had been facing mental health issues. She had recently stayed at Vinod’s room and was reportedly planning to travel with him to a temple in Tamil Nadu. items.title: Kerala is now officially ‘Keralam’ as Union govt notifies name change
items.summary: Kerala is officially ‘Keralam’ with effect from August 25 after the Union Home Ministry notified the new name of the southern state and brought the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026 into force. The notification comes just ahead of Onam, which is the traditional harvest festival of Kerala and one of the state’s most widely celebrated festivals. In a gazette notification issued on Tuesday, August 25, the Home Ministry said, “In exercise of the powers conferred by sub-section (2) of Section 1 of the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act, 2026, the Central government hereby appoints the 25th day of August, 2026, as the date on which the provisions of the said Act shall come into force.” President Droupadi Murmu had earlier this month given her assent to the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill, turning it into law. The Lok Sabha passed the Bill on August 11, followed by the Rajya Sabha on August 12. Minister of State for Home Affairs Nityanand Rai said during the Rajya Sabha debate that the Kerala Assembly had passed a resolution in 2024 urging the Union government to change the state’s name to Keralam. “The Bill provides that the State of Kerala will be known as the State of Keralam, and hence there is a proposal to rename Kerala to Keralam,” Nityanand Rai said. The Kerala government had forwarded the Assembly’s resolution to the Union government in June 2024. Subsequently, President Murmu referred the Bill to the state legislature for its views, following which the Assembly adopted a unanimous resolution agreeing with the proposal. The name-change process was initiated after the Kerala Legislative Assembly passed a resolution on June 24, 2024, seeking to replace ‘Kerala’ with ‘Keralam’, the name used in Malayalam. The Union Cabinet approved the proposal in February 2026, after which the legislative process moved forward. The Kerala (Alteration of Name) Act provides for the change of the state’s name to Keralam and makes the necessary consequential amendments to the Constitution. The legislation was introduced in Parliament after the state legislature’s views were obtained under the constitutional procedure for altering a state’s name. The change means that the name ‘Keralam’ will now be used officially in place of ‘Kerala’ in relevant government and constitutional references. The change follows the Assembly’s resolution that the state’s name in Malayalam is Keralam.

items.title: ‘Troubling to see rise of exclusionary movement’: Mamdani opposes Mohan Bhagwat’s NYC event
items.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, on Tuesday, August 25, said he does not support the planned Madison Square Garden event where Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) chief Mohan Bhagwat is scheduled to address members of the Indian diaspora, but said he was unsure whether the city had the authority to cancel a private event. Bhagwat is scheduled to address around 5,000 people at Madison Square Garden on Saturday, August 29, as part of the RSS’s centenary-year global outreach programme. He arrived in the United States on Tuesday and is also expected to participate in the Universal Oneness programme during his stay in New York. Mamdani said at a news conference, “I don't support the rally, but I don't know if the city has any jurisdiction on cancelling a private event.” His remarks came in response to questions about the RSS, the planned Madison Square Garden event and protests against Bhagwat’s appearance. Mamdani, who is the first Indian-American mayor in New York City’s history, also referred to his family background while explaining his opposition to the event. He said , “I also stand here as the first Indian-American Mayor in our city's history, and my mother's family is all still in India.” He said the vision of India he had learnt from his family was that of a society that embraced people from different backgrounds. Mamdani described that vision as “a pluralistic society, of a secular republic that believed in the belonging of each and every person who was from India”. He went on to criticise what he described as the rise of an exclusionary political movement. Mamdani said , “it has been incredibly troubling to see the rise of a movement that is predicated on an exclusionary vision of any country”. He said he was therefore opposed to the movement both as an Indian-American and as the mayor of a city that, he said, believes in the inclusion of people irrespective of their identity. He said, “I find myself in deep opposition to, not only as an Indian-American but also as the Mayor of a city that believes deeply in the belonging of each and every person, no matter their colour, their creed, their religion, their faith, wherever they're from.” The planned event has also drawn opposition from several interfaith and civil rights organisations in New York. Groups including Hindus for Human Rights, the Indian American Muslim Council and the Interfaith Centre of New York held a press conference outside New York City Hall and urged Madison Square Garden to cancel

items.title: ‘Not bothered about personalities’: Madras HC warns CM Vijay, Min Aadhav Arjuna
items.summary: The Madras High Court, on Tuesday, August 25, warned Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and Public Works Minister Aadhav Arjuna that it could impose an exemplary cost of Rs 50,000 each if they sought further adjournment to file applications seeking rejection of election petitions challenging their victories in the 2026 Assembly elections. Justice V Lakshminarayanan issued the warning while hearing the election petitions concerning Vijay’s victories from the Perambur and Tiruchirappalli East constituencies and Aadhav Arjuna’s victory from Villivakkam. According to LiveLaw , Justice Lakshminarayanan orally remarked, “I'm not bothered about the personalities. You people say that election cases are not being decided. But then you are asking time. Election petitions are to be disposed of within 6 months.” The judge stressed that the court was working within the statutory six-month period for disposing of election petitions and therefore could not permit prolonged adjournments. The judge also observed that obtaining the affidavits signed by the concerned parties would not take much time. Counsel appearing for Vijay and Aadhav Arjuna submitted that the applications seeking rejection of the election petitions were ready, but there had been a delay in obtaining the signatures of the two leaders due to the ongoing Assembly session. The counsel sought more time and requested the court not to impose costs. The counsel assured the court that the applications would be filed within two days. The court, considering the assurance, refrained from imposing costs for the time being and adjourned the matter. The counsel later assured the court that the applications seeking rejection of the plaints would be filed in a day, following which the court adjourned the matter to August 27. The election petitions were filed challenging the victories of Vijay and Aadhav Arjuna in the recent Assembly polls. The Madras High Court had admitted the petitions in July and emphasised that election petitions were required to be decided as expeditiously as possible and within six months. Three of the four election petitions against Vijay challenge his victory from the Perambur Assembly constituency, while another challenges his victory from the Tiruchirappalli East constituency. The Perambur petitions were filed by DMK candidate RD Shekar and voters Dinesh and Lakshmi Narasimman. DMK candidate Inigo Irudayaraj filed an election petition challenging Vijay’s victory from Tiruchirappalli East
